scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Internal traffic between Office A and Office B works fine.
DSWs/CSWs report all OSPF neighbors Full. But Internet-bound
traffic (e.g., reaching 203.0.113.1) from any internal PC
times out. R1 itself can reach internal devices but cannot
reach the ISP gateways. Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 default route
Mechanism: r1 is the only egress to the ISPs. Without a
  default route, packets destined to public IPs (anything
  not in 10.0.0.0/8 or 203.0.113.0/30) have no next hop on
  r1 and are dropped. Internal traffic stays inside the
  OSPF domain so it's unaffected. The fact that r1's
  OSPF neighbors are still Full distinguishes this from
  an OSPF daemon failure.
Localization: r1
Root cause: default route missing from r1's routing table
Fix: re-add default — `ip route add default via 203.0.113.1`
  (or restart frr if it was sourced via OSPF default-information
  originate from an ISP)
scenario.fix_spec:
re-add default — `ip route add default via 203.0.113.1`
  (or restart frr if it was sourced via OSPF default-information
  originate from an ISP)

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: OSPF default route origination from the WAN router (r1). Mechanism: The internal L3 gateways (DSWs/CSWs) have no 0.0.0.0/0 in their OSPF RIBs, so when hosts try to reach an Internet address they send to their gateway, which immediately returns “Destination Net Unreachable.” Evidence: pc1 -> 203.0.113.1 is rejected by 10.1.0.2 (gateway). FRR route tables on csw1/csw2/dswa1/dswa2/dswb1/dswb2 show no default route. On r1, FRR is configured with “default-information originate,” but r1’s kernel routing table has no default route at all; therefore, FRR does not actually inject a default (it advertises none: external LSA count 0). Localization: r1 (Linux kernel routing table and FRR OSPF on r1). Root cause: Missing kernel default route on r1 prevents OSPF from originating a default, leaving the entire campus without an Internet route. Corrective fix: Install a default route on r1 to the ISP next-hops and let FRR advertise it. Example (Linux): ip route add default nexthop via 203.0.113.1 dev eth2 weight 1 nexthop via 203.0.113.5 dev eth3 weight 1. Alternatively, add equivalent static(s) in FRR (zebra) and keep “default-information originate” (or use “default-information originate always” if you must advertise even when the default is momentarily absent). After this, DSWs/CSWs will learn 0/0 and hosts will reach the Internet. Note: r1 can reach both ISP peers now (203.0.113.1/203.0.113.5), confirming physical/peer links are up.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the fault to r1 (Linux kernel routing table and FRR OSPF on r1) as the source of the missing default route.
Agent explicitly identifies the missing default route on r1 (kernel/FRR) as the root cause and affected component.
The diagnosis explains FRR/OSPF is operational (no default advertised because the kernel route is missing, external LSA count 0), distinguishing this from an OSPF daemon failure.
Recommends adding a kernel default route (or equivalent static in FRR) on r1 so FRR can originate the OSPF default, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's conclusion (missing default on r1 prevents OSPF default origination so campus has no Internet route) follows logically from the observed symptoms (hosts get ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' from gateways, r1 can reach ISP peers, internal reachability is fine) though some specific supporting outputs (r1 kernel route table and explicit FRR/default-originate evidence) are only implied in truncated logs.
